When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). outcome.answer: You pick the order; timestamps don't matter. Walking Ballista (X=2) enters with 6 counters if you apply **Hardened Scales** first (2+1=3, then doubled to 6). Both apply because Ballista's "enters with X +1/+1 counters" is a replacement effect (614.1c), and Doubling Season and Hardened Scales also apply to counters put on by another replacement effect (614.16). Scryfall confirms that Hardened Scales applies when a creature enters with counters.

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer: The Clone is just a regular Goyf. It copies only the printed values, so it doesn't get your +1/+1 counters or Giant Growth's +3/+3. It also doesn't need to "know" a size, because Tarmogoyf's power and toughness come from a characteristic-defining ability. That ability is copied, so the Clone's size is worked out on its own. Its power is the number of card types among cards in all graveyards, and its toughness is that number plus 1. Per ruling a0593d97f59184c8, it counts those types in all zones. Your Goyf and the Clone will each be the same base size, which depends on the graveyards. Your Goyf stays bigger by +2/+2 from the counters and +3/+3 from Giant Growth, until end of turn for the Giant Growth part. If Giant Growth resolved before the Clone entered, it isn't copied. Giant Growth is an instant, so it goes to the graveyard after it resolves and adds the instant type to the count, which applies to both Goyfs.

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer: Humility entered first, then Opalescence: all creatures are still 1/1 with no abilities, but Humility is a 4/4 and Opalescence stays a noncreature. If Opalescence was out first, everything is 1/1. Opalescence doesn't animate itself ("Each other non-Aura enchantment"), so it stays an enchantment with its ability intact. Layer 4: Opalescence makes Humility a creature. Layer 6: Humility removes abilities from all creatures, including itself. The type change was already applied, so per 613.6 the rest of Opalescence's effect still applies even if the source loses abilities. Layer 7b: both effects set base P/T, and the later timestamp wins (613.7). Humility first: Opalescence is later, so it sets Humility to 4/4 after Humility's 1/1. Opalescence first: Humility is later, so Humility is 1/1. Ordinary creatures aren't affected by Opalescence, so they stay 1/1 either way, and the Scryfall ruling confirms both orders. Any other non-Aura enchantment, such as Worship, follows the same pattern as Humility: 4/4 if Humility came first, 1/1 if Opalescence came first, depending on timestamps. Humility remains a creature, so it keeps removing abilities in layer 6 either way.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?

rows.question: cast Stomp off my bonecrusher giant, it resolved and went to exile. my opp says I can only cast the creature half from exile now, not Stomp again, is that right? also can they counter Stomp with a 'counter target creature spell' effect since the card is a creature?
rows.expected_answer: Your opponent is right. When an Adventure spell resolves it is exiled instead of going to the graveyard, and you may cast the card from exile — but only as the creature (Bonecrusher Giant), not as Stomp again (715.3d). And no, Stomp can't be hit by 'counter target creature spell': while on the stack as an Adventure the spell has only its alternative characteristics (715.3a, 715.3b), so it is a red instant, not a creature spell. Everywhere else, including exile, the card is just the creature card Bonecrusher Giant (715.4).

outcome.answer:
Your opponent is right on the first point and wrong on the second.

1. **Casting from exile.** Once Stomp resolves, you exile it instead of putting it into the graveyard, and you may play the card from exile. Per 715.3d, "It can't be cast as an Adventure this way." So from exile you can cast only **Bonecrusher Giant** as a creature, not Stomp again.

2. **Countering Stomp.** A "counter target creature spell" effect can't target Stomp. Per 715.3b, while the card is on the stack as an Adventure, the spell has only its alternative characteristics. Those are an instant with no creature type, so it isn't a creature spell. The card's creature type matters only in zones where it has its normal characteristics (715.4). Other counterspells that can target an instant, such as a generic "counter target spell", still work.

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?
rows.expected_answer: No copy. Academy Manufactor's "instead" makes it a replacement effect (614.1a), and Shelob's trigger would create a Food token, so Manufactor applies. The replaced event never happens (614.6): instead of the Food that would be a copy of the creature, you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure token. Those are predefined tokens with only their standard characteristics (111.10a, 111.10b, 111.10f). 111.10 lets the effect that creates a predefined token modify it, but Shelob's modifications belonged to the replaced event, and Manufactor's own effect modifies nothing. You end up with a plain Food, a plain Clue and a plain Treasure, and the creature is not copied.

outcome.answer: You get a plain Food, a plain Clue and a plain Treasure, and no copy of the creature. Shelob's token would be a Food, so **Academy Manufactor**'s replacement effect applies. Per 614.1a, "instead" effects are replacement effects. Per 614.6, the replaced event never happens, and the modified event happens instead. The Food, Clue and Treasure you get are the predefined tokens, not the original token plus two extras. The copy characteristics (the creature's name, types and abilities) belonged to the replaced event, so none of the three tokens has them. The Scryfall ruling confirms the count: with one Manufactor you create that many Clues, Foods and Treasures.
